# What new constraint does artificial regeneration impose on modified cells?

Watch thousands of plantlets growing inside glass jars under laboratory lights, where chemical signals drive rapid cell multiplication.

When cells divide at high speeds without the normal regulatory checks of an intact plant body, copying errors accumulate in their DNA.

Many regenerated plants show visible defects, stunted leaf shapes, or loss of fertility—a phenomenon known as somaclonal variation.

Exploiting developmental flexibility frees us from natural growth limits, but it strips away the organism's natural safeguards that preserve genetic stability across cell generations.
